original.target_description: Unassigned original side; placeholder only. Original primary source was not assigned or inspected.

replication.target_description: Primary random-effects meta-analysis across 22 eligible labs of average hostility ratings of five ambiguously hostile behaviors, comparing 80%-hostile minus 20%-hostile sentence primes; immediate testing, 30 sentences.

n.sample_role: Analytic participants across 22 laboratories; 2,813 in 20%-hostile and 2,797 in 80%-hostile condition.
n.exclusions: Individual exclusions: incomplete sentence-descrambling task or critical ratings, nonstudents, age outside 18–25, missing gender, failure to follow instructions or other experimenter-recorded reasons. Four labs with fewer than 100 participants per condition excluded from primary analyses; 22 labs retained. N counts participants, not the 22 laboratory estimates.

notes: Identity independently checked: title Registered Replication Report on Srull and Wyer (1979), McCarthy et al. author list, 2018, Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science 1(3), 321–336, DOI 10.1177/2515245918777487 all match the replication reference. University of Groningen cover labels this Publisher’s PDF/Version of record; supplied text includes article pages 321–336, methods, results, figures, discussion, and references, rather than an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF path supplied. Original reference is not this primary work and is unassigned. Target chosen by outcome identity: description names interpretations of ambiguous behaviours, matching the five-behavior hostility-rating outcome (Fig. 2), rather than the separate Ronald trait-rating outcome (Fig. 1). Locator p.7 introduces both outcomes; primary behavior estimate continues on printed p.328 and Fig.2 on p.329. Primary conditions are mutually exclusive randomized 20%-hostile and 80%-hostile groups. Analytic participant N = 2,813 + 2,797 = 5,610; 22 labs are the meta-analytic units. This agrees with the abstract’s directly reported primary-analysis N. Retain printed raw mean difference −0.08 scale points, not d. The approximately d = 0.06 printed on p.332 explicitly concerns the positive Ronald-rating effect, so it does not apply to the behavior outcome. Same-test p is not printed: 95% CI [−0.18, 0.01] is given; p = .27 belongs to Q(21) = 24.39 heterogeneity. Ancillary all-lab behavior result is −0.10, N = 6,404; it is distinct from the primary 22-lab analysis and is not substituted. Author narrative verdict coded failed because authors say their procedures are unlikely to produce practically/routinely detectable assimilative priming; not inferred solely from significance.
